title: Small filtered category of finitely presented module pairs over a quasi-coherent sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] which is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. There exist a set $I$, sheaves $\mathcal G_i$ of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] for $i\in I$, and $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps $\alpha_i:\mathcal G_i\to\mathcal F$, with the following properties. For every sheaf $\mathcal G$ of finite presentation and every $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\psi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$, there are $i\in I$ and an isomorphism $e:\mathcal G_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G$ such that $\psi\circ e=\alpha_i$. Define $\mathcal I$ to have object set $I$ and morphism sets $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal I}(i,j)=\{u:\mathcal G_i\to\mathcal G_j\text{ $\mathcal O_X$-linear}\mid\alpha_j\circ u=\alpha_i\},$$ with the identities and composition of module maps. Then $\mathcal I$ is a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: it is nonempty, every two objects map to a common object, and for all parallel arrows $a,b:i\to j$ there are an object $k$ and an arrow $v:j\to k$ with $v\circ a=v\circ b$. The assignments $M(i)=\mathcal G_i$ and $M(u)=u$ define a functor $M:\mathcal I\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, and the maps $\alpha_i$ form a cocone from $M$ to $\mathcal F$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-presentation-representatives] to obtain a set $J$ of finite-presentation modules $P_j$ representing all such modules. Morphisms are families of linear maps on the set of opens satisfying restriction equations [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], hence each $\operatorname{Hom}(P_j,\mathcal F)$ is a set. Put $I=\coprod_{j\in J}\operatorname{Hom}(P_j,\mathcal F)$, $\mathcal G_{(j,f)}=P_j$, and $\alpha_{(j,f)}=f$. Given $(\mathcal G,\psi)$, choose $e:P_j\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G$ and take $i=(j,\psi e)$; then $\alpha_i=\psi e$, as required.

proof.text: The displayed Hom sets are subsets of the module-morphism sets, hence sets. Identities satisfy $\alpha_i\mathrm{id}=\alpha_i$, and if $\alpha_j u=\alpha_i$ and $\alpha_k v=\alpha_j$, then $\alpha_k(vu)=\alpha_i$; associativity and unit laws are those of module maps [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus this is a small category. The zero module has the rank-zero local presentation $0\to0\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]; representing its zero map to $\mathcal F$ gives an object, so $I$ is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 01PJ, lemma-directed-colimit-diagram-finite-presentation, proof, choice of pairs and filteredness, lines 3066-3120; the commuting-triangle equation is read in the type-correct order.

proof.text: For $i,j$, let $B=\mathcal G_i\oplus\mathcal G_j$, which is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-presentation-direct-sum]. Using the biproduct maps [def-weil-additive-category], set $h=\alpha_i p_i+\alpha_j p_j:B\to\mathcal F$; the biproduct identities give $h\iota_i=\alpha_i$ and $h\iota_j=\alpha_j$. Step 1 supplies $e:\mathcal G_k\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ with $he=\alpha_k$. The maps $e^{-1}\iota_i$ and $e^{-1}\iota_j$ therefore define arrows $i\to k$ and $j\to k$.

source.place: Tag 01PJ, lemma-directed-colimit-diagram-finite-presentation, proof, choice of pairs and filteredness, lines 3066-3120; the commuting-triangle equation is read in the type-correct order.

proof.text: For parallel arrows $a,b:i\to j$, take $q:\mathcal G_j\to Q=\operatorname{Coker}(a-b)$ in the abelian module category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Both modules are of finite presentation, so [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-presentation-cokernel] makes $Q$ finitely presented. Since $\alpha_j(a-b)=\alpha_i-\alpha_i=0$, the cokernel universal property gives $h:Q\to\mathcal F$ with $hq=\alpha_j$. Step 1 gives $e:\mathcal G_k\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$ with $he=\alpha_k$. Put $v=e^{-1}q$. Then $\alpha_kv=\alpha_j$ and $v(a-b)=e^{-1}q(a-b)=0$, hence $va=vb$. This is the required arrow $j\to k$.

source.place: Tag 01PJ, lemma-directed-colimit-diagram-finite-presentation, proof, choice of pairs and filteredness, lines 3066-3120; the commuting-triangle equation is read in the type-correct order.

proof.text: Steps 2-4 verify precisely the three filteredness conditions of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Define $M$ on objects by $i\mapsto\mathcal G_i$ and on arrows by their underlying module maps. The identities and composition chosen in Step 2 give the functor laws. Every arrow satisfies $\alpha_jM(u)=\alpha_i$ by its defining equation, so $(\mathcal F,(\alpha_i))$ is a cocone by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

lean.statement: theorem exists_finitePresentation_pairs_filtered (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] : ∃ (I : Type u) (G : I → X.Modules) (α : ∀ i : I, G i ⟶ F), (∀ i : I, (G i).IsFinitePresentation) ∧ (∀ (H : X.Modules), H.IsFinitePresentation → ∀ ψ : H ⟶ F, ∃ (i : I) (e : G i ≅ H), e.hom ≫ ψ = α i) ∧ IsFiltered (ModulePairIndex α)
